quests.instruction: A square is turned so that one corner points straight up. What shape is it now?
options: A rhombus, no longer a square
quests.hint: Turning moves a shape around. Does it change the sides or the corners?
quests.explanation: Turning does not change the number of sides, how long they are, or how the corners look. A square turned on a corner still has four equal sides and four square corners.
quests.funFact: A baseball infield is a square, but because it is drawn with a corner at the bottom, people call it a diamond.

quests.instruction: Which of these does turning a shape change?
quests.hint: Think about what stays the same when you spin a shape on a table.
quests.explanation: Turning changes the direction the corners point. The number of sides and their lengths stay exactly the same.
quests.funFact: A shape that is moved without changing its size or form is said to be congruent to the original.

quests.instruction: A yield sign has three equal sides and points downward. If it is turned so one corner points up, what shape is it?
quests.correctAnswer: A triangle with three equal sides
options: A triangle with three equal sides
quests.hint: Count the sides and corners after the turn.
quests.explanation: Turning does not add or remove sides. The sign still has three equal sides and three corners, so it is the same triangle.
quests.funFact: Yield signs point downward in many countries, which makes them stand out from other triangular signs.

quests.instruction: A clock's minute hand points straight up at 12. It makes a quarter turn clockwise. Which number does it point to now?
quests.hint: A full turn goes all the way around, so a quarter turn goes a quarter of the way.
quests.explanation: Clockwise is the way clock hands move. A quarter of the way around from 12 lands on the 3.
quests.funFact: A clock face is divided into 12 equal parts, so a quarter turn covers 3 of them.

quests.instruction: A signpost arrow points to the right. A student gives it a half turn. Which way does it point now?
quests.hint: A half turn is two quarter turns, or halfway around.
quests.explanation: A half turn sends an arrow to the opposite direction, so right becomes left.
quests.funFact: A full turn brings an arrow back to where it began, and a half turn is exactly half of that.

quests.instruction: A toy car on a map faces north. It makes a quarter turn counterclockwise. Which way does it face now?
quests.hint: Counterclockwise is the opposite way to clock hands. Picture a compass.
quests.explanation: Turning counterclockwise from north goes toward the left side of the compass, which is west.
quests.funFact: A compass needle points north because it lines up with Earth's magnetic field.

quests.instruction: Which shape looks exactly the same after a half turn?
options: A right triangle with a square corner at the bottom left
quests.hint: Picture the shape upside down and compare it with how it started.
quests.explanation: A rectangle has matching opposite sides and corners, so turned upside down it looks the same. A triangle that pointed up now points down, and the right triangle's square corner moves.
quests.funFact: Shapes that look the same after a half turn are said to have rotational symmetry.

quests.instruction: After a quarter turn, which shape looks exactly the same as before?
quests.hint: A quarter turn swaps a shape's width and height. Which shape has equal width and height?
quests.explanation: A square has four equal sides and four square corners, so a quarter turn leaves it looking unchanged. A long, thin rectangle would turn from wide to tall.
quests.funFact: A square looks the same after every quarter turn, so it fits into a square hole four different ways.

quests.instruction: A regular pentagon has one corner pointing up. After a half turn, does it look the same?
options: Yes, it looks exactly the same
Yes, but only if it is also flipped
quests.hint: Look at where the single corner at the top ends up.
quests.explanation: A regular pentagon has an odd number of sides, so a half turn sends its top corner to the bottom and a flat side to the top. It is the same pentagon, but it looks different.
quests.funFact: A regular pentagon looks the same after one fifth of a full turn, five times around.

quests.instruction: The letter b is flipped like a mirror, left to right. Which letter does it look like?
quests.hint: Imagine the stem of the b standing on the right side instead of the left.
quests.explanation: A left to right flip puts the stem on the right and the round part on the left, which makes a d.
quests.funFact: Many children mix up b and d because each one is the mirror image of the other.

quests.instruction: A right triangle has its square corner at the bottom left. It is flipped left to right like a mirror. Where is the square corner now?
quests.hint: A left to right flip swaps the left and right sides but leaves top and bottom alone.
quests.explanation: The flip swaps left and right, so a corner at the bottom left moves to the bottom right while staying at the bottom.
quests.funFact: A mirror image has the same size and shape as the original but faces the opposite way.

quests.instruction: Which shape looks exactly the same after a left to right flip?
quests.correctAnswer: A triangle with two equal sides, pointing up
options: A right triangle with a square corner at the bottom left
A triangle with two equal sides, pointing up
quests.hint: Imagine a mirror standing down the middle. Does each side match the other?
quests.explanation: A triangle with two equal sides pointing up is balanced, so its left and right sides match. The right triangle and the letter F lean to one side.
quests.funFact: A shape that matches itself when flipped is said to have a line of symmetry.

quests.instruction: Which move can change a right triangle's square corner from the bottom left to the bottom right?
quests.correctAnswer: A flip from left to right
options: A flip from left to right
quests.hint: Think about which moves change the direction a shape faces, not just where it sits.
quests.explanation: Only a flip puts the corner on the opposite side while keeping it at the bottom. Sliding changes position only, and making the triangle bigger does not move the corner.
quests.funFact: A slide, a turn, and a flip are the three basic ways to move a shape without changing its size.

quests.instruction: One letter b is given a half turn. Another letter b is flipped upside down like a mirror under it. Do they look the same?
quests.correctAnswer: No, one looks like q and the other like p
options: No, one looks like q and the other like p
quests.hint: Work out each result separately before you compare them.
quests.explanation: A half turn changes b into q, but a top to bottom flip changes b into p. A turn and a flip are different moves.
quests.funFact: The letters p and q are also mirror images of each other.

quests.instruction: Which change alters the shape itself, not just where it sits or which way it faces?
quests.hint: Think about which move changes the length of a side.
quests.explanation: Stretching changes side lengths, so the shape changes. Turning and flipping only change position and direction.
quests.funFact: A move that keeps size and shape the same is called a rigid motion.

quests.instruction: A shape sits on one corner. It has four equal sides, and every corner looks like the corner of a book page. Which shape is it?
quests.hint: Use the clues about sides and corners. The way the shape sits does not matter.
quests.explanation: Four equal sides and four square corners make a square, even when it sits on a corner. A leaning rhombus has no square corners, and a long rectangle has no equal sides.
quests.funFact: A chessboard turned so a corner points at you still has the same squares.

quests.instruction: A shape sits with one corner at the bottom. It has four equal sides, but its top and bottom corners are sharper than its side corners. Which shape is it?
quests.hint: Compare the corners with the corner of a book page, however the shape is turned.
quests.explanation: A shape with four equal sides and corners that are not square is a rhombus. A square has square corners, and a kite does not have four equal sides.
quests.funFact: A rhombus can be built from two equal triangles joined along a side.

quests.instruction: A regular hexagon is first drawn with a flat side on top. It is then turned so that a corner is on top. What is the second drawing?
quests.hint: Turning cannot add or remove sides.
quests.explanation: A turn does not change how many sides a shape has. It still has six equal sides, so it is the same hexagon.
quests.funFact: Pencils with six sides are easy to grip and do not roll off a desk as easily as round ones.

quests.instruction: A ladder with two parallel side rails stands against a wall. It is then laid flat on the ground. Are the rails still parallel?
quests.correctAnswer: Yes, turning does not change that
options: Yes, turning does not change that
quests.hint: Think about whether moving the ladder bends or changes the rails.
quests.explanation: Parallel sides stay the same distance apart wherever the object is placed. Moving or turning it does not change that.
quests.funFact: Ladder rungs are spaced evenly so each step is the same height.

quests.instruction: Which uppercase letter looks exactly the same after a half turn?
quests.hint: Picture the letter upside down, then compare it with the original.
quests.explanation: Turned upside down, the diagonal in N still runs the same way and the two sides swap places, so it looks unchanged. P and E look different upside down.
quests.funFact: The word SWIMS reads the same when it is turned upside down.

quests.instruction: A tablet is held upright, then turned sideways. What changes about its screen?
quests.hint: Turning moves a shape but does not stretch it.
quests.explanation: When the tablet is turned, the long side moves from vertical to horizontal, so a different side is on top. The sides keep their lengths, and the screen keeps four corners.
quests.funFact: Phones and tablets sense when they are turned and rotate the picture to match.

quests.instruction: An arrow points up. It makes a quarter turn clockwise, and then another quarter turn clockwise. Which way does it point now?
quests.hint: Two quarter turns make a half turn.
quests.explanation: The first quarter turn points the arrow right, and the second points it down.
quests.funFact: Four quarter turns make a full turn and bring the arrow back to the start.

quests.instruction: A letter p is given a half turn. Which letter does it look like?
quests.hint: A half turn sends the stem from the left to the right and from the bottom to the top.
quests.explanation: A half turn moves the stem to the right side and the round part to the left, which makes a d.
quests.funFact: The letters b, d, p, and q are all made from the same stem and round part placed in four different ways.

quests.instruction: A right triangle has its square corner at the bottom left. It makes a quarter turn clockwise. Where is the square corner now?
quests.hint: Clockwise means the way clock hands move. Follow the corner one quarter of the way around.
quests.explanation: Moving the bottom left corner a quarter turn clockwise carries it up to the top left.
quests.funFact: Following one corner is an easy way to track a turn.

quests.instruction: Two triangles both have sides of 3 cm, 4 cm, and 5 cm. In one, the 5 cm side is at the bottom. In the other, the 5 cm side is on the left. Are they the same size and shape?
options: No, the sides are different lengths
quests.hint: Compare the side lengths, not where the sides sit.
quests.explanation: Both triangles have the same three side lengths, so they are the same triangle. One has simply been turned.
quests.funFact: A triangle with sides of 3, 4, and 5 has a square corner, and builders use this to check corners.

quests.instruction: Which pair shows the same shape and size, with one just turned?
quests.correctAnswer: A 6 cm by 2 cm rectangle and a 2 cm by 6 cm rectangle
options: A 6 cm by 2 cm rectangle and a 6 cm by 3 cm rectangle
A 6 cm by 2 cm rectangle and a 2 cm by 6 cm rectangle
A 6 cm by 2 cm rectangle and a 4 cm by 4 cm square
quests.hint: Look for a pair with the same two side lengths.
quests.explanation: A 2 cm by 6 cm rectangle is a 6 cm by 2 cm rectangle turned a quarter turn. The other pairs have different side lengths.
quests.funFact: A sheet of paper can be held tall or wide, and it is the same sheet both ways.

quests.instruction: Which pair shows the same shape and size, where one is a mirror flip of the other?
quests.correctAnswer: Two equal right triangles facing opposite ways
options: A big square and a small square
Two equal right triangles facing opposite ways
quests.hint: A mirror flip keeps size and shape but reverses the direction.
quests.explanation: Two equal right triangles facing opposite ways are mirror images of each other. A big and a small square differ in size, and a triangle and a rectangle differ in shape.
quests.funFact: Your left and right hands are mirror images of each other.

quests.instruction: Mira turns a square a quarter turn, then flips it over. Is it still the same size and shape?
options: No, turning makes it a rhombus
quests.hint: Think about what a turn and a flip each change.
quests.explanation: A turn and a flip only change position and direction. The square keeps its size, its four equal sides, and its four square corners.
quests.funFact: People check whether two shapes match by imagining one laid on top of the other after turning or flipping it.

quests.instruction: Which shape looks different after a half turn but is still the same shape?
quests.correctAnswer: A triangle with equal sides, pointing up
options: A triangle with equal sides, pointing up
quests.hint: Find the shape that would look different upside down.
quests.explanation: A triangle pointing up points down after a half turn, so it looks different, though it is the same triangle. A rectangle and a circle look unchanged.
quests.funFact: A shape can look different from different angles and still be exactly the same shape.

quests.instruction: Jo says: When I turn a rectangle, its sides get shorter. What is wrong with her idea?
quests.correctAnswer: Turning does not change the length of the sides
options: Turning does not change the length of the sides
quests.hint: Think about what happens to a ruler if you spin it on a table.
quests.explanation: Turning only changes which way a shape faces. Its side lengths stay exactly the same.
quests.funFact: A part keeps its size however it is rotated, which engineers rely on when they design machines.
